title: Investors Challenge $2T Anthropic Valuation in Bid for Largest IPO
summary:
Market participants are debating the cost of the AI company's shares as rising interest rates increase the overhead of data center operations. While bankers floated a $2T valuation, some prospective investors suggest the firm is worth closer to $1.5T, though others have discussed a range between $1.8T and $2T for the Nasdaq listing. The debut involves Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citi, and could surpass SpaceX's $86B raise to become the largest IPO in history.

Anthropic targets a listing in mid-November to incorporate third-quarter financial results, with marketing potentially starting the week of Nov 9 and shares trading before Nov 26. A confidential S-1 filing from June 1 lists infrastructure commitments with Broadcom and Amazon and warns of existential risks to humanity from the company's most advanced models. This trajectory follows a May private round that raised $65B at a $965B valuation and contrasts with rival OpenAI's decision to postpone its own debut until 2027.

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic's IPO date has moved three times in two months. Here is every rumor, in order.

What is confirmed:

- Anthropic filed a confidential draft S-1 with the SEC on June 1
- Its last private round, in May, raised $65B at a $965B post-money valuation

The timeline, as it keeps slipping:

- August: the FT reports an October listing
- September 5: Bloomberg says marketing starts mid-October at the earliest, with a listing just before the midterms
- September 18: the WSJ reports a push to November, so the offering can include Q3 results
- October 1: Bloomberg says marketing could begin the week of November 9
- That moves the listing past the November 3 midterm election
- A follow-up report says Anthropic meets prospective investors on October 14

The deal, as reported:

- Exchange: Nasdaq, per Business Insider. The same venue that landed SpaceX
- Banks: Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citi
- Valuation: up to $2T, with some shareholders talking about $3T
- Anthropic's executives have not set a number, per the FT
- Size: aiming to match or top SpaceX's record $86B raise, per Bloomberg
- It is reportedly weighing letting existing shareholders sell in the offering
- First it is finalizing a $15B revolving credit facility. Then analysts meet management

The numbers investors are hearing:

- Q2 revenue above $11.5B, roughly 14x a year earlier
- Positive adjusted operating income in Q2
- Investors told to expect a second profitable quarter in Q3
- Backers expect a $100B to $120B run rate by year end

The noise around it:

- The WSJ reported in August that pre-IPO meetings had become confidence-building sessions
- OpenAI pushed its own IPO to 2027 last month, leaving Anthropic first in line
- In late September, an appeals court sided with the Pentagon in its supply-chain risk dispute with Anthropic
- Dario Amodei had his first one-on-one dinner with Trump on September 27

The frame: every slip so far has a stated reason, from Q3 numbers to a credit line.

But each delay also gives public markets more time to decide what a frontier lab is worth.

Mid-November is now the date to watch.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Anthropic's IPO now has a rough calendar. Here is what moved in the last week.

The new timeline:

- Bloomberg says marketing could begin the week of November 9
- Shares could start trading before Thanksgiving on November 26
- Prospective investors reportedly meet the company on October 14
- The October target slipped so the offering can include Q3 numbers

The price talk:

- Prospective investors have discussed $1.8T to $2T, per Bloomberg
- Anything above SpaceX's $1.78T debut makes it the largest IPO ever

Then Reuters got the prospectus:

- Reuters says it obtained a copy of Anthropic's confidential S-1
- 2025 revenue grew roughly 12x, to about $4.6B
- The filing warns of "existential risks to humanity" from its most advanced models
- It also details large infrastructure commitments with Broadcom, Amazon and others

Who is watching closely:

- SK Telecom, an early investor, says it has no plans to sell its stake immediately
- There is still no word on how much of the offering, if any, goes to retail
- Forbes reports retail money flooding into pre-IPO funds charging up to 3% in fees
- One of those funds holds no Anthropic shares at all

The bull case, from CFRA analyst Angelo Zino: "very strong appetite and demand for Anthropic."

The frame: a lab whose CEO asked the industry to slow down is about to ask Wall Street for up to $2T.

And its own filing lists existential risk as a disclosure. Investors will have to price that too.
